item.title: Google debuts 'Create My Widget' AI tool for custom home screen widgets on Pixel devices
item.description:
Google debuts ‘Create My Widget’ AI tool for custom home screen widgets on Pixel devices

Google has introduced Create My Widget, an AI-powered feature that lets Pixel users design custom home screen widgets through natural language prompts. The tool, part of Android’s Gemini Intelligence suite, is currently in beta and rolling out to Pixel phones.

📱 What Can You Build?

Create My Widget enables users to generate a variety of functional widgets including:

  • Weather-based messages (e.g., “Tut tut, looks like rain” when precipitation is detected)
  • Entertainment displays (like hourly Jurassic Park quotes from the original film)
  • Personal habit trackers (such as logging daily mental health walks)
  • Event countdowns (counting down to holidays or calendar events)
  • Sports updates (showing recent scores and upcoming game times)
  • Recipe suggestions (daily three-ingredient cocktail ideas)

⚙️ How It Works

The feature operates as a prompt shortcut for Gemini. When you tap a created widget, it opens the Gemini interface on your home screen, processes your request, and generates the desired output. Some examples:

Widget Type Functionality
Quote Widget Displays a different Jurassic Park quote each hour
Weather Widget Shows “Tut tut, looks like rain” during precipitation, “No rain right now” otherwise
Walk Logger Triggers Gemini to add a walk to calendar and provides a checklist for marking completed walks
Bus Schedule Searches for arrival times at a specified stop (though results vary in usefulness)

🚀 Availability and Limitations

  • Currently in beta testing
  • Rolling out to Pixel phones (tested on Pixel 11 Pro)
  • Creation time: approximately 20 seconds per widget
  • Not a one-size-fits-all solution—some use cases like real-time transit data produce less useful outputs

#GoogleAI #Android #Gemini #Widgets #Pixel

Source: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun

item.title: Signal Adds Protections Blocking AI Assistant Screen Access on iOS and Android
item.description:
Signal Adds Protections Blocking AI Assistant Screen Access on iOS and Android

Signal has announced new protections that block screenshots on iOS 27 and prevent AI assistants from capturing conversations on supported Android devices. These measures are designed to stop built-in AI assistants, such as Siri and Gemini, from accessing private conversation content while performing tasks for users.

🔍 Overview

The announcement follows Signal’s introduction of a feature in May 2025 that blocked Microsoft’s Recall screenshot-capturing feature on Windows 11. Signal’s president, Meredith Whittaker, stated that the company is now taking similar measures to restrict agentic systems built into iOS 17 and on Android versions where an AI assistant attempting to read the Signal screen can be detected.

Signal engineers spent months investigating how AI systems access app data. They designed targeted protections to block all extraction pathways, which were verified through reverse engineering. The protections specifically target OS-level features like Siri’s Onscreen Awareness and Google’s Gemini Intelligence, which can otherwise capture chat content as it appears on the screen.

⚙️ Key Details

The new protections operate differently across platforms:

  • iOS: The protection blocks screenshots entirely. This includes preventing users from taking screenshots of Signal conversations for legitimate purposes. On the iOS app, users can verify that “Block Siri AI” is enabled by navigating to Settings > App Security.
  • Android: Signal automatically enables Screen Security when it detects an AI assistant attempting to access the screen.
  • macOS: Signal is currently unable to provide screenshot-blocking protection for macOS. For macOS 27 users, Signal recommends adding the app to the Excluded Apps list under System Settings > Siri to prevent proactive access to message content.

Signal notes that the protections are automatically activated when possible, though specific app version numbers were not provided.

💡 Why it Matters

Signal warns that AI agents embedded deep in operating systems pose an “existential threat” because they can access conversation data through methods beyond simple screen reading. Whittaker notes that these vulnerabilities leave apps with limited options for protecting users and expose sensitive private data belonging to all conversation participants.

In response, Signal is calling on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide detailed documentation disclosing all potential access mechanisms. The company urges these operating system vendors to give developers a clear way to opt out of AI access across screens, files, notifications, and APIs.

#Signal #Privacy #AIAgents #Security #iOS #Android

Source: Signal to block Siri, Gemini AI from capturing chats on iOS, Android

item.title: Stable Diffusion runs on Android via Snapdragon NPU acceleration
item.description:
Stable Diffusion runs on Android via Snapdragon NPU acceleration

📢 Overview

Run Stable Diffusion on Android devices using Snapdragon NPU acceleration. This project is now open-sourced and completely free, supporting both NPU and CPU/GPU inference paths.

🧩 How It Works

Local Dream is built on top of many excellent open-source projects, including:

Component Function
Qualcomm QNN SDK NPU model execution
alibaba/MNN CPU model execution
happyyzy/stable-diffusion.cpp Deep performance optimizations for on-device DiT inference
xtensor-stack Tensor operations & scheduling
mlc-ai/tokenizers-cpp Text tokenization
yhirose/cpp-httplib HTTP server
nothings/stb Image processing
facebook/zstd Model compression
nlohmann/json JSON processing
square/okhttp HTTP client
coil-kt/coil Image loading & processing
MoyuruAizawa/Cropify Image cropping
AOSP, Material Design, Jetpack Compose UI framework
CompVis/stable-diffusion Base model framework
xinhtao/Real-ESRGAN Image upscaling
Kim2091/UltraSharpV2 Image upscaling
bhky/opennsfw2 NSFW content filtering

⚙️ Key Details

  • Currently focused on SD1.5 and SDXL models.
  • SD2.1 is no longer maintained due to poor quality and limited popularity.
  • SD1.5 models are supported on Snapdragon NPUs with Hexagon V68 architecture or newer.
  • SDXL models are supported on Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 and newer devices.
  • CPU/GPU inference supports SD1.5 and imported SDXL MNN packages.
  • Large SDXL models require substantially more memory than SD1.5.

💬 Community

  • You can join the Local Dream telegram group for discussion or help with testing.

#StableDiffusion #Android #Snapdragon #NPU #OpenSource

Source: xororz/local-dream

item.title: BADBOX 3.0 Botnet Returns with Record Ad Fraud Activity
item.description:
BADBOX 3.0 Botnet Returns with Record Ad Fraud Activity

The BADBOX malware botnet has resurfaced, generating a record 40 billion fraudulent advertising bid requests per day through infected Android-based devices.

🔍 Overview

  • The BADBOX 3.0 variant has grown into the largest documented ad-fraud operation by daily bid request volume.
  • It was first discovered in early 2023 on a T95 Android TV box bought on Amazon.
  • Germany’s cybersecurity agencies warned in December 2024 that the botnet had infected tens of thousands of devices.
  • In March 2025, a large-scale disruption operation took place where HUMAN and Shadowserver cut off more than 500,000 BADBOX 2.0 devices from their control servers, while Google removed 24 apps that spread the malware from Google Play.
  • Google later sued the botnet’s operators, saying the BADBOX 2.0 had infected over 10 million Android-based devices by April 2025.

🧩 How it works

  • The malware performs ad fraud by playing video ads in hidden windows while impersonating legitimate streaming apps to make the requests appear legitimate.
  • HUMAN also observed fraudulent server-side ad insertion (SSAI) requests that tricked advertisers into believing ads were played on streaming devices, even though no actual device or video ad was involved.
  • A proxying module also enrolled infected devices in one of 11 residential proxy networks without the owners’ knowledge or consent.
  • One of those networks, PXYEDGE, was identified as the rebranded successor to IpMoYu, a residential proxy service previously linked to BADBOX 2.0.
  • The researchers say PXYEDGE advertised approximately 200,000 proxy nodes, while their monitoring showed unique connections peaking at around 340,000.
  • HUMAN says some of the ad fraud traffic was also routed through these residential proxies to appear legitimate and evade anti-abuse filters.

⚙️ Key details

  • The infected devices fetch malware modules from public code repositories, while the same payloads are also mirrored across various hosting platforms for redundancy and to resist takedowns.
  • HUMAN says it also participated in Google’s disruption of the related XCPE malware operation earlier this month, which included taking down multiple C2 domains used by BADBOX 3.0.
  • Additionally, one of the malware repositories was taken down, while HUMAN says its systems now filter fraudulent advertising traffic associated with BADBOX 3.0.

💡 Why it matters

  • Users should only buy certified Android devices from reputable manufacturers and ensure that Play Protect is available and active.

#BADBOX #Malware #AdFraud #Android #Cybersecurity

Source: BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking 40 billion daily ad requests

item.title: Signal blocks screenshots on mobile to stop AI agents reading messages
item.description:
Signal blocks screenshots on mobile to stop AI agents reading messages

Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices to prevent AI agents from reading users’ messages and other data.

🧩 How it works

Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen. The company is addressing privacy concerns by blocking the ability to take screenshots in the app on iOS 27 and Android, which should prevent Siri, Gemini, and other Android AI assistants from reading on-screen content. Users can restore screenshot capabilities in Signal’s app settings, but the president warns that doing so will “potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Limitations: The screenshot-blocking remedy is “incomplete” as it does not address alternative ways that AI agents can access app data, such as retrieving it via the device file system.
  • Platform Availability: Signal is currently unable to implement these protections on macOS.
  • Previous Precedent: Signal took a similar approach last year to prevent Microsoft’s controversial Recall feature from capturing secured chats.
  • Developer Tools: The service is struggling to develop a better solution due to the lack of available information regarding how AI agents are actually accessing application data.
  • Ecosystem Call: Signal is calling on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide “simple technical tools and accurate documentation” to app developers. More tools are also needed to prevent third-party agents, like Meta’s Muse, from using deep accessibility settings in apps like a “skeleton key” to access application data.

💡 Why it matters

Signal president Meredith Whittaker stated that the agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are “undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.” She urged OS providers to make it easier for app developers to control what data agents can access. Whittaker emphasized: “We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy.”

Whittaker noted that even where they are able to detect and block AI data access, major tech companies do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. She concluded: “We all need to recognize that the current integration of AI agents into the operating system, without these common-sense remedies, represents an existential threat to privacy at the application layer, and the ability of independent developers like Signal to protect your sensitive data,” adding that “Signal is the canary in the coal mine, but this affects the entire ecosystem and should galvanize anyone who cares about these fundamental rights.”

#Signal #AIAgents #Privacy #iOS27 #Android

Source: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen

item.title: Android adds Gemini‑AI‑powered enhanced protection to Google Messages
item.description:
Android adds Gemini‑AI‑powered enhanced protection to Google Messages

Android is introducing new scam defense features that aim to make it easier for users to evade mobile fraud, including bolstered protection in Google Messages and additional safeguarding tools.

🔍 Overview

  • Android is using AI to suss out scammers in Google Messages.
  • A new “enhanced protection” setting will roll out in the coming weeks and is opt‑in.

🧩 How it works

  • The enhanced protection mode taps into cloud‑based Gemini AI models to quickly evaluate a potential scammer’s intentions in conversations with an unrecognized sender.
  • “Scammers often disguise their true motives behind slow‑burn conversations,” Google said.
  • “This secure cloud analysis augments and extends our existing on‑device detection, allowing us to identify novel and sophisticated attacks, actively uncovering and stopping abusers who try to hide their tracks.”
  • User data is encrypted during this AI analysis and processed in a secure dedicated space that Google (and anyone else besides the user) can’t access.
  • The mode also uses on‑device Gemini Nano AI to inspect real‑time web signals in unfamiliar URLs before they are opened to determine if the links are malicious.

⚙️ New security features

Feature Description
Call‑forwarding block Blocks apps from enabling call forwarding and notifies the user when someone attempts to do so.
Screen‑share privacy Automatically conceals sensitive information while screen‑sharing in Chrome and Android WebView.
Enhanced protection Opt‑in mode that uses Gemini AI to assess intentions of unrecognized senders and scans URLs with Gemini Nano.

🌐 Expansion and rollout

  • The scam detection feature for chat notifications that Google introduced on Pixel phones last year is expanding to devices from Honor, Motorola, Oppo, OnePlus, Realme, Tecno, Vivo, Xiaomi, and more.
  • Google says it plans to bring it to “hundreds of millions of additional users later this year.”

#Android #AI #Security #ScamDetection

Source: Android is using AI to suss out scammers in Google Messages

item.title: Google allows users to launch personal AI apps through Play Store
item.description:
Google allows users to launch personal AI apps through Play Store

Google has announced a new feature in the US that allows users to launch personal, vibe-coded apps directly through the Google Play Store.

🧩 How it works

  • Apps are launched using a standard Google account.
  • The feature is separate from the public store catalog, keeping the apps secure and private.
  • Users will soon have the ability to share these apps with a select group of people.

⚙️ Key details

  • Google first introduced the ability to vibe-code personal Android apps in May.
  • If users wish to share their app with the world, they can transition to a professional developer account.
  • Professional accounts are subject to the same Trust & Safety reviews and quality standards as existing professional developers, according to Sam Bright, Google’s vice president and general manager of Google Play.

🚀 Availability

  • This feature is currently available in the US.

#GooglePlay #Android #AppDevelopment #TechNews

Source: Google makes it easier to launch your vibe-coded apps

item.title: Google pushes Android 17 developer preview with battery and privacy enhancements
item.description:
Google pushes Android 17 developer preview with battery and privacy enhancements

The Android ecosystem is busy this weekend as Google released a fresh update to the Android 17 developer preview, focusing on better battery life, background‑process control, and new privacy tweaks.

🔍 Overview

  • Android 17 developer preview arrives with a revamped battery settings menu.
  • Users can now see which background services consume the most power.
  • A new Private Space folder lets you hide specific apps from the app drawer without uninstalling them.
  • Notification snooze lets you silence alerts for one or two hours.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Battery Management
    • Revamped battery settings menu.
    • Visibility of power‑hungry background services.
  • App Privacy
    • Hide apps in the Private Space folder.
    • Google aims to help users find apps that behave badly.
  • Notification Control
    • Swipe a notification to the side for a snooze option.

📱 Additional Android Updates

  • Google Maps – Minor update adds the ability to save multiple custom routes as home‑screen shortcuts.
  • Google Photos – Refresh includes a faster search index for quicker object and person searches.
  • Security Patch – October security patch released for all supported Pixel devices, fixing three major flaws that could allow unauthorized media‑file access. Other manufacturers (OnePlus, Motorola) expected to roll it out by mid‑next week.

🚀 Availability

  • The Android 17 preview is now available for developers.
  • Google plans to open the beta to more devices soon.
  • Reminder: Back up your data before installing major system updates; keeping copies of photos and documents is always wise.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Improved battery visibility helps users extend device runtime.
  • Enhanced privacy controls give users more granular app management.
  • Faster search in Google Photos and custom route shortcuts in Maps streamline everyday tasks.
  • The October security patch addresses critical vulnerabilities, reinforcing device security across the ecosystem.

#android #android17 #mobileupdates #privacy #security

Source: Android Daily News: October 10, 2026 – Latest Updates and Releases - thetechpapa

item.title: Google's Gemini AI to Automate Personal Phone Calls with 'Call for Me' Expansion
item.description:
Google’s Gemini AI to Automate Personal Phone Calls with ‘Call for Me’ Expansion

Google may be expanding its “Call for Me” AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family.

🔍 Overview

Android Authority reports a “Gemini Calling” introductory screen in an APK teardown. The screen shows example prompts such as:

Example Prompt Intended Action
Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late Deliver a quick voice message to a family member
Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner Deliver a quick voice message to a friend

These examples suggest the feature would allow users to dictate short, text‑message‑style calls.

🧩 How it Works

  • Users issue a spoken prompt to Gemini (e.g., “Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late”).
  • Gemini generates a brief spoken message based on the prompt.
  • The AI places a phone call and plays the generated message, reaching the recipient without the user having to speak.
  • Android Authority also found “granular permissions” for Gemini actions in individual apps, including phone‑call permissions, letting users control which apps can invoke the feature.

⚙️ Key Details

  • The rumored Android update would automate personal phone calls with Gemini AI.
  • Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late, or deliver other short updates.
  • Even with this expansion, Gemini would likely be limited to basic, text‑message‑like calls; it is not expected to conduct full, back‑and‑forth conversations.
  • Users could opt out of receiving incoming automated calls from Gemini via the granular permission settings.
  • Android Authority notes Google might choose not to publicly release the expansion or the permission controls.

🚀 Availability

  • The feature is currently rumored and has been observed in an APK teardown; no official release date or public announcement has been confirmed.

💡 Why it Matters

  • It offers a quick way to reach people who prefer phone calls, miss text messages, or still use landline phones.
  • The granular permission model could give users fine‑grained control over AI‑driven calling capabilities on Android devices.
  • If released, the feature would extend Google’s AI services from business contexts into everyday personal communication.

#Google #Gemini #AI #Android #CallForMe

Source: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late

item.title: Introduction of Docker-Android for Android Development and Testing
item.description:
Introduction of Docker-Android for Android Development and Testing

Docker-Android is a docker image designed to support all aspects of Android development and testing, including native, web, and hybrid-app projects.

⚙️ Key details

Docker-Android provides the following capabilities:

  • Ability to build Android projects.
  • Execution of unit and UI-Tests using frameworks such as Espresso and Appium.
  • VNC support to view the inside of the docker container.
  • Log sharing feature via a web-UI.
  • External control of the emulator using adb connect.
  • Integration with cloud solutions, including Genymotion Cloud.
  • Support for mcp server (beta-version).

🚀 Availability

Various image tags are available:

  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_9.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_10.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_11.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_12.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_13.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_14.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:genymotion
